state.objective: Challenge the proposed fixed-asset COA compression and identify the next COA area to review after the bank stage.
confirmed_facts: Current working baseline after the bank-name compression proposal is 488 account families.

The client has 57 asset-cost families, 20 accumulated depreciation/amortization families, 20 depreciation/amortization expense families, 36 Reserve Replacement OE families, plus unresolved CIP, HGB, pre-opening and Disposed Inventory accounts.

Round 1 concluded with high confidence that asset_id and associated_site_id belong in an asset register, cost/accumulated/expense remain separate natures, owned land remains separate, CIP remains separate, and HGB/pre-opening/Reserve Replacement OE/Disposed Inventory require evidence.
Round 1 preferred broad asset classes over one fixed-asset account or all 57 cost accounts. It was uncertain on compressing 36 OE items, seven FFE classes, and depreciation-expense detail.
No asset ledger, useful-life policy, materiality thresholds, transactions, balances, financial-statement notes or tax-book requirements have been supplied.
state.guardrail: Choose what the evidence supports. Do not calculate the total COA count; arithmetic will be performed outside Jev. Repeated model answers are judgments, not accounting evidence.

next_domain.instructions: After bank identity has been reviewed, which listed domain is the strongest next candidate for dimensional compression based on the supplied COA structure?

criteria.fixed_assets: Asset item identity repeats across cost, accumulated depreciation and expense and can be governed by an asset register.
criteria.receivables: Review customer identity and receivable types next, despite no receivable evidence in this state.
criteria.payables: Review supplier identity and payable types next, despite no payable evidence in this state.
criteria.revenue_expense: Compress revenue and expense categories next, despite no such evidence in this state.

broad_classes_gate.instructions: Are the proposed broad classes a final migration mapping now, or only a design hypothesis pending client records and policy?

criteria.conditional: Use as a target hypothesis; approve mappings only after register, policy, balances and reconciliation.

building_three_to_one.instructions: Can Bangunan Utama, Bangunan Tambahan and Staff House/Mess use one building-cost GL plus asset_class_id if ownership, useful-life policy and reporting treatment are aligned?

criteria.conditional_merge: Yes, subject to aligned policy and reporting.
criteria.retain: They must always remain three GLs.

machine_four_to_one.instructions: Can AC, Lift, Eskalator and Genset use one machinery/equipment cost GL plus asset_class_id when useful lives and reporting treatment are controlled in the register?

criteria.conditional_merge: Yes, if accounting policy and reporting can be reconciled by class.
criteria.retain: They must always remain four GLs.

vehicles_two_to_one.instructions: Can Mobil and Sepeda Motor use one vehicle-cost GL plus asset_class_id when depreciation and reporting are reconciled by class?

criteria.conditional_merge: Yes, subject to policy and reporting alignment.
criteria.retain: They must always remain separate GLs.

software_two_to_one.instructions: Can Seventh Soft and Opti Tex use one software-cost GL plus asset_id/application type if both are capitalized software under the same accounting policy?

criteria.conditional_merge: Yes, subject to capitalization/useful-life policy and reconciliation.
criteria.retain: Each application name must remain a GL.
criteria.immediate: Merge now solely from the names.

parallel_mapping.instructions: If a cost class is merged conditionally, should its accumulated depreciation and depreciation expense normally follow the same class mapping while staying separate natural-account natures?

criteria.yes: Use parallel class mapping across cost, accumulated and expense, with separate natural accounts.
criteria.no: Class mapping should be unrelated across the three natures.
criteria.one_account: Combine all three natures into one GL.

oe_without_accumulated.instructions: Does the absence of explicit accumulated-depreciation accounts for 36 OE cost families support merging them immediately?

criteria.no: It increases the need to inspect postings and the Reserve Replacement OE mechanism first.
criteria.yes: Absence proves they can be merged now.
criteria.expense: Absence proves all OE is expense.

reserve_posting_test.instructions: What evidence is most decisive for classifying the 36 Reserve Replacement OE accounts?

criteria.entries_policy: Sample journal entries, normal balances, counterpart accounts, policy and balance roll-forward.
criteria.asset_list: Physical asset list alone without postings.

expense_detail_gate.instructions: Before reducing 20 depreciation/amortization expense families, what should determine whether broad expense GLs still meet reporting needs?

criteria.reporting_reconciliation: Management/statutory reporting requirements plus reliable asset-class reporting and reconciliation.
criteria.count_target: The desire to reach a target account count.

safe_now.instructions: Given the missing records, what may be approved now?

criteria.architecture_only: Approve asset_id, asset_class_id and associated_site_id architecture; keep GL merges conditional.
criteria.all_merges: Approve every proposed asset merge now.
criteria.nothing: Do not even design the asset-register dimensions.

repeat_answers_limit.instructions: Can repeated Jev judgments replace client accounting policy, register reconciliation and transaction evidence for final migration?

criteria.no: Jev can structure hypotheses and gates but cannot replace the records.
criteria.yes: Repeated model agreement is sufficient evidence.
